claims.text: Adding approximately 0.5–1 wt% Y to an HEA bond coat will improve coating durability and reliability relative to an undoped bond coat.
Y added to the HEA bond coat is expected to segregate to grain boundaries and/or the oxide–bond-coat interface.
Y segregation will promote formation of a more adherent oxide scale.
Y segregation will promote formation of a denser oxide scale.
Y segregation will promote formation of a more stable alumina or related oxide scale.
Y reduces the lateral growth rate of oxide grains.
Y enhances oxide-scale adhesion by modifying interfacial chemistry.
Y retards the formation of defects that lead to oxide-scale spallation.
The proposed reactive-element effects will slow oxidation degradation under cyclic thermal stresses.
Y-doped HEA bond coats will have higher oxide-scale adhesion than the untreated baseline during high-temperature exposure and thermal cycling.
Y-doped HEA bond coats will have lower spallation rates than the untreated baseline during high-temperature exposure and thermal cycling.
The improvement is expected to persist under high-temperature oxidation and thermal-cycling conditions typical of TBC service.
Effectiveness outside the stated TBC service conditions has not been established.
The magnitude of the improvement and the optimal Y concentration within 0.5–1 wt% are unknown and require experimental validation.
